headline: GOLD ENDS WEEK AT $4,420 AS NFP BLOWOUT PUSHES RATE-HIKE ODDS TO 60% — CPI SEPT 12 IS THE NEW FULCRUM
snippet: Gold finished Friday at $4,420/oz — down 1.28% on the session — after August nonfarm payrolls came in at 162,000, more than double the 56,000 consensus, shattering the soft-landing narrative that had briefly pushed rate-hike odds to 50/50. With unemployment holding at 4.1%, markets priced a near-60% probability of a Fed hike at the September 15–16 FOMC. Markets are now closed through the weekend; the August CPI print on September 12 arrives just four days before the FOMC decision and is the single print that will determine whether gold tests $4,136 support or makes a run at $4,700.

headline: STANMORE RESOURCES ACQUIRES MORANBAH SOUTH FROM EXXARO FOR US$105M — 743MT OF QUEENSLAND MET COAL; ASX: SMR
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) announced September 5 it will acquire the Moranbah South (MBS) metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million (approximately R1.68 billion). Exxaro first exercised joint-venture pre-emptive rights to buy Anglo American's 50% interest in the MBS JV — triggered by Anglo's sale of Australian coal assets to Dhilmar QLD — then flipped the asset to Stanmore. The MBS resource stands at 743 million tonnes, including 505Mt at 18.5% volatile matter. Deal closes Q4 2026 subject to Australian regulatory approvals.

headline: ANGLO-TECK $53B COPPER MEGA-MERGER WAITS ON BEIJING — CHINA ANTITRUST SOLE HOLDOUT AS SEPT–MARCH WINDOW OPENS
snippet: The proposed Anglo American–Teck Resources all-share 'merger of equals,' announced September 9, 2025, has now cleared every major jurisdiction — Canada, Chile, Australia, Japan, the EU, and the U.S. — leaving China and South Korea as the final regulatory hurdles. Anglo American says it expects the outstanding decisions between September 2026 and March 2027. The combined entity would carry a market value of approximately $53 billion, with Teck valued at roughly $24 billion including debt, creating a global powerhouse in copper, iron ore, and zinc. China's review carries particular weight: it consumes approximately half of global refined copper output annually.

headline: VALE SHELVES BASE METALS IPO — BRAZIL KILLS CRITICAL MINERALS SPINOFF CITING SOVEREIGNTY CONCERNS
snippet: Vale has shelved plans to list Vale Base Metals (VBM) — its London-based copper, nickel, and cobalt subsidiary carved out in 2023 — after political opposition in Brazil made a public offering untenable. CEO Shaun Usmar had said in March 2026 that VBM would be ready for a potential IPO by midyear; that deadline has passed. Brazilian officials raised concerns about losing state influence over strategic mineral assets including nickel and cobalt operations spanning Canada, Brazil, Japan, the UK, and Indonesia. VBM could still pursue a listing at a later date, per sources, but no timeline was provided.

headline: USA RARE EARTH COMPLETES SERRA VERDE MERGER — FIRST INTEGRATED RE+MAGNET PLATFORM OUTSIDE ASIA; NASDAQ: USAR
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) completed its combination with Serra Verde Group on September 3, 2026, creating what the company describes as the first fully integrated rare earth mining and permanent magnet manufacturing platform outside Asia. Serra Verde's operation in Goiás, Brazil began production in January 2024 and is completing its optimization phase, with Stage 1 targeting approximately 4,000 tonnes per annum of total rare earth oxide output by end 2026. The combined entity spans the full value chain from mine to magnet — an architecture that no single Western-controlled company has previously achieved.

headline: ARAFURA BREAKS GROUND ON NOLANS BORE — AUSTRALIA'S FIRST ORE-TO-OXIDE NdPr OPERATION ENTERS CONSTRUCTION
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths has commenced construction at its Nolans Bore NdPr oxide project in Australia's Northern Territory, following the May 21, 2026 Final Investment Decision. When complete, Nolans will produce 4,440 tonnes per annum of neodymium-praseodymium oxide — a critical feedstock for rare earth permanent magnets used in EVs, wind turbines, and defence systems — making it Australia's first fully integrated ore-to-oxide rare earth operation. Hatch leads engineering, procurement, and construction management. Export Finance Australia has indicated non-binding support for up to 500 tpa of NdPr oxide output. First production is targeted for mid-2029.

headline: CONGO EXTENDS COPPER AND COBALT CONCENTRATE EXPORT BAN TO SEPTEMBER — COBALT SURGES AS SMELTERS SCRAMBLE FOR FEED
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo has extended its ban on copper and cobalt concentrate exports — originally signed June 29 — through September, sending cobalt prices surging as smelters scramble for alternative feed. Goldman Sachs notes the direct impact on refined copper is limited: DRC exported 696,725 tonnes of copper cathodes in Q1 2026 compared to just 53,926 tonnes of concentrate (containing roughly 18,863 tonnes of copper metal). But the extension adds meaningful supply tension for Chinese and European smelters already competing for shrinking global concentrate supply, with Chilean output down 9.4% year-on-year and Peruvian disruptions ongoing.

headline: URANIUM REBOUNDS TO $82 AS MINERS SURGE 17-21% — WNA DOUBLES DEMAND FORECAST TO 2040; CAMECO SIGNALS TIGHTER SUPPLY
snippet: Uranium spot prices have rebounded to approximately $82/lb — up roughly 8% from recent lows near $79.60 — as investor conviction returned to the sector in early September. The Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index gained 17.01% in the month with junior miners up 21.75%, outpacing equities and commodities broadly. The World Nuclear Association's latest forecast projects reactor requirements to more than double by 2040, boosted by small modular reactors and new entrants including Microsoft. Supply remains structurally constrained: Cameco flagged McArthur River disruptions from May flooding while Kazatomprom cut its 2026 production guidance by approximately 10%.

headline: SILVERCORP HALVES CHINA OUTPUT — YING AND GC MINES DOWN 40-50% ON SAFETY CRACKDOWN THROUGH SEPTEMBER; NYSE: SVM
snippet: Silvercorp Metals (NYSE: SVM / TSX: SVM) has been operating at significantly reduced capacity at its Ying and GC mines in China since late June, after national regulators launched cross-sector safety inspections following a fatal coal mine accident in Shanxi Province. Ying production has fallen 40–50% and GC approximately 50% for the July–September quarter, at a direct cost of roughly US$11.5 million in safety upgrades. Ying normally produces approximately 6.3 million ounces of silver annually. Management expects 10–15% residual impact in the October–December quarter as phased operational approvals are processed, with the safety system upgrades to be completed by local certified vendors.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES' SUREBET SWELLS TO 2.01 km² — 7.38 g/t AuEq OVER 35.7m AS 50,000m GOLDEN TRIANGLE PROGRAM ROLLS ON; GOT
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSXV: GOT / OTCQX: GOTRF) continues to expand the Surebet high-grade gold discovery in British Columbia's Golden Triangle with 52 of 98 planned holes drilled and 31,994 metres completed of a 50,000-metre program running seven drill rigs. Best hole of the 2026 season: GD-26-436 returned 7.38 g/t AuEq over 35.7 metres, including 19.51 g/t AuEq over 8.32 metres. Visible gold has been confirmed in 33 of 52 completed holes. The discovery footprint has grown 12% to 2.01 km² as the team drills volcanic wedge zones connecting the Bonanza and Golden Gate zones. More results are pending from holes 53 through 98.

headline: JP MORGAN TARGETS $6,000 GOLD BY YEAR-END — $1,100 ABOVE GOLDMAN'S FRESHLY CUT FORECAST, CENTRAL BANK BUYING CITED
snippet: J.P. Morgan Global Research analysts see gold pushing $6,000/oz by year-end 2026, with $6,300/oz a possibility for 2027 — a dramatically more bullish view than Goldman Sachs, which freshly cut its year-end target to $4,900 last week. The divergence hinges on central bank behaviour: JP Morgan argues that sovereign reserve diversification away from dollar-denominated assets is a structural, multi-year driver that rate cycles cannot extinguish. Even in a higher-for-longer rate environment, JP Morgan expects institutional and sovereign demand to absorb gold at current levels and then some.

headline: SILVER HEADS FOR SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT YEAR AT 215M OZ RECORD — SOLAR, EV, AI DEMAND OUTPACING MINE SUPPLY
snippet: The Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual silver supply deficit in 2026, this time at an estimated 215 million ounces — the largest on record. Total silver supply is forecast to rise just 1.5% to 1.05 billion ounces, with mine production growing only 1% to 820 million oz, a pace structurally outpaced by industrial consumption from solar panels, EVs, and AI data-centre backup systems. China, already the world's largest silver consumer, imported 790-plus tonnes in early 2026. Silver has averaged approximately $74/oz year-to-date — up 116% versus the same period in 2025 — yet the structural deficit math suggests price discovery is far from complete.
